description: Re-escalation of the US-Iran confrontation around the Strait of Hormuz: the 60-day ceasefire expired and a tanker was seized in the Strait on 2026-08-17/18, followed by tougher US sanctions on Iran. Brent held ~$94/bbl (2026-08-24) and WTI above $84.50 with supply-disruption risk repricing. This is a NEW discrete development on the same driver as cat_20260228_hormuz_closure (archived, fully priced-in): that event documented the February closure; this one captures the August ceasefire breakdown, which was partially expected (markets stayed notably bullish per BofA FMS 2026-08-18).

strength_anchors.note: Rubric total 65 (str_01+str_02+str_04): ~20% of world oil flows is in scope and the US naval blockade is a decided action, but the escalation was not a consensus surprise and it is a level shift in supply, not a rate. Stored 68 sits inside the bracket. Backfilled 2026-10-17.

review_log.evidence: WTI rose from USD 91.09 on 2026-10-08 to USD 101.37 on 2026-10-16 (+3.4 that day) on risk of US escalation in Iran; Trump said on 2026-10-08 no attack before the 2026-11-03 midterms while the US naval blockade stays in force; Iran's Mehr agency denies a deal. Stored event records Brent ~94 on 2026-08-24, so the oil level has moved well beyond it. Re-verify on 2026-11-03.

Brent settled ~103 USD after Trump said on ~2026-10-08 the US will not attack Iran before the 2026-11-03 midterms while the naval blockade 'remains in full force'; WTI 95.12 on 2026-10-14. Sources conflict on the level (89 vs 103; one result showing 83 is an April-dated page and was discarded). Brent is therefore elevated but the escalation risk has a stated pause until 2026-11-03, which is the date to re-verify. sector_impact BACKFILLED: oil_majors_integrated supportive, eu_defense_prime_contractors supportive. Not registered as a new event or an oil structural: same economic driver as this event, and the energy shock is also the cause of cat_20260617_fed_hawkish_pivot / cat_20260916_fed_rate_hike (a second oil catalyst would double count).
